newsitem.title: GERMANY: Peru finance minister sees Brady debt deal by Dec.
newsitem.headline: Peru finance minister sees Brady debt deal by Dec.

text.p: Peru will complete by December a Brady refinancing of its commercial debt with a 59 percent reduction, Finance Minister Jorge Camet said on Thursday.

Peru has been working with J.P. Morgan on the plan, and has succeeded in cutting its external debt to $20 billion from $26 billion, said Camet, who is in Germany for four days with President Alberto Fujimori on an investment mission.
"In December we will have the closing. There has been some adjustment because the debt has been broken in many small pieces," he said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.

Complex interest calculations have delayed the deal, which financial markets have been expecting since July, he said. "If we don't finish ... by December we will make an escrow deposit. We must finish in December"
Last month, Peru formally proposed to its bank creditors a $2.482 billion buyback at the closing of its Brady plan to restructure $10.657 billion of foreign debt.
"What cost 100 is now costing 41 for us, so (it is) a reduction of 59 percent," he said.
After the restructuring is set, Peru plans to make a bond issue on international markets early next year, he said, but declined to comment on the terms.
Peru has sought to brake its economy from the 8.3 percent average growth over the past three years to an expected "soft landing" of three percent this year.

"To grow too much increases our current-account deficit. This could be dangerous. That's why we cooled the economy," Camet said. At the same time, it strove to avoid the contractions seen in Mexico and Argentina recently.
Peru's growth should rebound to five to six percent annually in the next few years, he added.
But it must also return to peace. A 16-year fight with the Shining Path guerillas is subdued, but not yet ended.
"First we have to get pacification. Then we hope to achieve economic stability, and then social stability. This is our main goal now," he said.

Improvements in education, health care and economic management should help Peru reduce extreme poverty by half by the end of President Fujimori's second term in the year 2000, from 18 percent of the population now, he said.

The Peruvian delegation hoped to attract German interest in Peru's privatisation programme, which has already attracted U.S., Spanish, Chinese and Chilean investors, but it has received no fresh commitments from Germany yet, he said.

Asked how he responds to recent criticism by Peruvian writer and one-time presidential candidate Maria Vargas Llosa of Fujimori's human rights record, Camet said, "I personally think Maria Vargas Llosa is an annoyed loser. He is very intelligent, but in this case he is not right."

Camet conceded that some human rights abuses have occured, but said they were unavoidable in the wartime conditions. A committee is reviewing claims of unfair imprisonment and 205 sentences are being corrected, he said.
Camet, who has served in Fujimori's cabinet for over four years, said he plans to remain in office one more year.
